nodes.label: 4-Week Plan
nodes.rationale: ~20 hrs/week with no buffer: if a week slips, cut UI polish, never verification. Week 1 skeleton+retrieval, Week 2 fan-out/fan-in, Week 3 writer+critic, Week 4 SSE+evals.

nodes.label: Versioned cache key scheme
nodes.rationale: search:v1:{provider}:{sha256(normQuery|freshness)[0:16]} and extract:v1:{sha256(normUrl)[0:16]}. Hashing exists only to give fixed-length, space-free, colon-free keys; correctness comes from the label containing everything that changes the upstream response.

nodes.label: Deviation: maxResults and minTier dropped from the search key
nodes.rationale: The implementation caches raw SearXNG results before tiering and filtering, so map/filter/limit run after the cache read. SearXNG ignores maxResults and has no concept of tiers, so neither can change the upstream bytes; including them would fetch identical data twice and burn a second credit. freshness stays because it maps to time_range and does change the response.

nodes.label: URL normalization rules
nodes.rationale: Lowercase host, strip fragment, strip utm_*/fbclid/gclid/ref, strip trailing slash, keep other query params and sort them alphabetically. Several spellings of one article then collapse to a single fetch, while ?page=1 and ?page=2 must stay distinct.

nodes.label: Query normalization rules
nodes.rationale: Lowercase, trim, collapse whitespace, keep quotes — quoted phrases are meaningful to the search engine so they must survive normalization.

nodes.label: Source tiering v1 (YAML domain allowlist)
nodes.rationale: Tiers 1-2 listed explicitly, default 3, tier 4 pattern-matched. Deliberately no LLM — trust classification must be cheap, deterministic, and editable.

nodes.label: Deviation: sidecar returns only OK | PAYWALLED
nodes.rationale: The sidecar is handed HTML and never fetches a URL, so it cannot observe UNREACHABLE, ROBOTS_DENIED, or TOO_LARGE — those are only visible at fetch time in Java. Keeping the sidecar fetch-free preserves the quota boundary.

nodes.label: Cache-aside written manually (no @Cacheable)
nodes.rationale: Explicit RedisTemplate get / miss / compute / set with TTL, serialized with Jackson not JDK serialization. The whole point is to write the pattern by hand once rather than take the framework shortcut.

nodes.label: Per-domain token bucket as a Redis Lua script
nodes.rationale: 1 rps, burst 3. GET-check-SET lets two researchers interleave between the read and the write and both pass the check; Redis executes a Lua script atomically so the check and the decrement cannot be split.

nodes.label: Parallel URL fetching with CompletableFuture
nodes.rationale: Each researcher fetches 5 URLs and sequential is 5x slower for no reason. allOf() to join and exceptionally() per future so one dead URL does not sink the batch; bounded by the extractor semaphore.

nodes.label: Cache stampede protection (single-flight lock)
nodes.rationale: Six researchers hitting the same uncached URL would fetch one page six times. SET key val NX PX 30000: the winner fetches, losers wait ~100ms and re-read cache. NX is the lock, PX is the safety valve so a crashed winner cannot deadlock everyone.

nodes.label: Semaphore(4) in front of the extractor sidecar
nodes.rationale: The sidecar falls over under 12 concurrent extractions; the bounded-resource pattern is roughly 10 lines. Release must be in a finally block or a leaked permit permanently shrinks the pool.

nodes.label: The researcher loop (one sub-question)
nodes.rationale: Eight steps from query generation to emitting a ResearchFinding, under hard limits of 90s wall clock, 25k tokens, and an allocated search budget. On breach it emits a partial finding with low confidence — partial is an explicitly valid outcome.

nodes.label: Flat fan-out (6-8 level-0 sub-questions)
nodes.rationale: The planner emits 6-8 sub-questions to research.subtasks with no dependencies, so all sit at level 0 and start immediately. depends_on/level columns are reserved but unused.

nodes.label: Fan-in SQL (UPDATE ... RETURNING on dag_levels)
nodes.rationale: Increment and read in one atomic statement so exactly one consumer observes completed == expected and triggers the writer, even if two researchers finish in the same millisecond.

nodes.label: Kafka consumer configuration for long-running work
nodes.rationale: Virtual threads enabled, listener concurrency 6, max-poll-records 1, max-poll-interval-ms 600000 — set before writing the consumer so subtasks are not evicted mid-work.

nodes.label: Fixture mode (replay recorded search + LLM responses)
nodes.rationale: A Spring profile replaying recorded responses from JSON gives zero-cost deterministic tests and is how the SSE page is developed in week 4 without burning credits.

nodes.label: Report / Section / Claim record contracts
nodes.rationale: Claim(text, sourceId, corroborating, kind) with ClaimKind FACT | FIGURE | QUOTE | INFERENCE. INFERENCE claims skip verification but must be visually distinct in output.

nodes.label: Critic loop and re-research gate
nodes.rationale: Load cached source text, chunk/embed/retrieve top-3 passages by cosine, grade with Haiku batched 10 per call, persist verdict plus exact passage. If unsupported_ratio > 0.15 and round < 2, re-research only the failed claims rather than the whole run. Deduping near-identical claims by embedding before verifying is a listed cost optimization.

nodes.label: SSE page (plain HTML, no framework)
nodes.rationale: Question input, live agent progress, per-claim badges; clicking a badge reveals the evidence passage. The passage is what makes verification credible, so it is explicitly not skippable.

nodes.label: Fabrication injection eval
nodes.rationale: Programmatically corrupt claims (SWAP_NUMBER, INVERT, SWAP_ENTITY, FABRICATE, OVERREACH), re-run the Critic, target catch rate >0.85 and false-positive rate <0.10. OVERREACH is called the hardest and most realistic category and must be included.

nodes.label: Speedup benchmark (concurrency 1 vs 6)
nodes.rationale: Hand-written ExecutorService + CountDownLatch harness so all threads start simultaneously and contention rather than ramp-up is measured. Expect ~2.7x not 6x because planner, writer, and critic are serial (Amdahl); claiming 6x signals you did not measure.

nodes.label: Restart-survival demo
nodes.rationale: Kill agent-service mid-run and restart: the run completes from committed Kafka offsets plus Postgres DAG state. Thirty seconds, and no in-process orchestration framework can do it.

nodes.label: Week 5 — Kubernetes + KEDA
nodes.rationale: A separate ~15-20 hr phase on a rented 8GB VM running k3s, gated on weeks 1-4 already working on Compose: don't containerize onto k8s something that isn't already correct.

nodes.label: Postgres/Redpanda/Redis stay as plain Docker, not in k3s
nodes.rationale: StatefulSets and PVCs on a single node are pure cost with no benefit at this scale; the three Java pods reach these over the VM's local network.

nodes.label: KEDA ScaledObject on agent-service only
nodes.rationale: agent-service is genuinely bursty (idle, then N researchers, then idle) and scales on research.subtasks consumer lag. retrieval-service and control-plane get fixed replicas because their load is steady — autoscaling everything is cargo culting.

nodes.label: Spring Security + JWT on control-plane only
nodes.rationale: control-plane is the only service with an ingress, so it is the only one needing auth. The others stay ClusterIP with no ingress: they need network isolation, not authentication. mTLS between three services on one node is theatre.

nodes.label: Three-layer rate limiting
nodes.rationale: Traefik middleware per IP stops raw flooding before any JVM; the per-domain token bucket protects search quota; the per-user daily run cap in control-plane matters most because the expensive unit is a run (~$0.04) not an HTTP request. The JWT sub claim keys the run cap — one credential, two jobs.

nodes.label: Explicitly not doing Eureka / service discovery
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes has service discovery built in and Compose resolves by service name; Eureka duplicates a platform feature, is a recognized anti-pattern, and adds a 4th deployable to an 8GB VM. Much of Spring Cloud Netflix is in maintenance mode.

nodes.label: OAuth2 Google login as a stretch goal
nodes.rationale: Being an OAuth2 client is an afternoon; being a provider (Spring Authorization Server) is a different project entirely. Skip if week 5 runs long — the JWT layer already secures the deployment.

nodes.label: CI/CD pipeline (moved to Week 5)
nodes.rationale: ci.yml build+test on PR with an eval gate so a prompt change regressing fabrication catch rate fails the build, publish.yml pushing SHA-tagged images to GHCR via Jib, deploy.yml using kubectl/helm from a self-hosted runner on the VM so the k8s API is never exposed.
